feedback.problem: The distance $d$, in meters, that a car has traveled after $t$ seconds can be modeled by the function $d(t)=\frac{2{t}^{3}+7t}{t+1}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the distance traveled when $t=2$ seconds?
feedback.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the distance traveled when $t=2$ seconds is equal to ${d}^{′}(2).$ 

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2{t}^{3}+7t}{t+1}) \\  & =\frac{(6{t}^{2}+7)(t+1)-(2{t}^{3}+7t)(1)}{(t+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{t}^{3}+6{t}^{2}+7}{(t+1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{d}^{′}(2) & =\frac{4(2)^{3}+6(2)^{2}+7}{((2)+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{32+24+7}{9} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the distance traveled when $t=2$ seconds is $7$ meters per second.
